chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Al-Mughira, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the man who divorces his wife while she is pregnant.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her waiting period (iddah) is that she gives birth to her child, and upon him is her maintenance (nafaqah) until she gives birth to her child.'

key_terms.تَضَعَ حَمْلَهَا: She gives birth to her child

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a pregnant divorced woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the prominent chain of Hammad ibn Isa, clarifies that the iddah for a pregnant divorcee extends until actual delivery rather than a fixed lunar period, ensuring continuous financial support (nafaqah) from the ex-husband. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the welfare of the mother and child during the transitional phase, linking the duration of maintenance directly to the biological event of childbirth.
